identity.purpose: Bodoni Moda identity lettering only; large masthead, film and footer wordmarks retain fixed-pixel graphic sizes, while the viewer identity is rem-based.

display.purpose: Source Serif 4 page titles for Latin/Cyrillic; regional Noto Serif for zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ja. The Bodoni homepage wordmark has separate fixed-pixel identity sizing.

headline.purpose: Locale-specific editorial serif headings at weight 600 with explicit responsive steps, separate from MOFER identity marks and third-level title exceptions.

title.purpose: Shared sans-serif h3 baseline; research activity titles are stronger, while object and theme titles use their component-specific serif roles.

body.purpose: Headings and editorial prose share Source Serif 4 for en/fr/de/es/ru and regional Noto Serif SC/TC/JP for CJK. The final prose rule uses --display, overriding earlier smaller local sizes; --body remains the inherited sans-serif interface family. Ordinary prose is 19px at the default root, 18px on phones, not a universal size for every visible word. Supported families and runtime samples do not establish universal glyph coverage.

label.purpose: Object type and exhibition status below a title, never a before-title kicker.

caption.purpose: Sans-serif reference text aligned to the printed mount's bounds. Gallery captions use this leading; viewer captions keep their own 1.5 leading, without a smaller phone size.

control.purpose: Primary and secondary text actions retain the default 16px size on phones; status/retry text remains a smaller utility exception.

navigation.purpose: Desktop route labels retain the default 16px size and wrap at enlarged text sizes; the compact disclosure uses a larger 1.1rem label. The header descriptor is hidden at all widths.

collection-title.purpose: Serif object names at weight 600, preceding 16px type metadata in selectable thumbnails; the phone title keeps its own size step.

identityProvenance.status: Existing Moving Archive identity, refined through a printed-album treatment under delegated user decisions. No replacement identity, new seed or approved visual comp is implied. The September 21 refinement is local only, after published editorial commit c204e1c.

fontDelivery.files: Package index.css, LICENSE copied as LICENSE.txt, and every supplied -wght-normal.woff2 file for each family.
fontDelivery.delivery: Local normal-variable faces retain Fontsource unicode-range subsets and font-display: swap. No runtime CDN or custom character subsetting.
fontDelivery.legacy: Committed assets/fonts are excluded from the build copy. The remaining Hanken development dependency is not a generated family or public type role.
fontDelivery.coverageScope: Source includes Cyrillic and Noto uses regional SC/TC/JP families. Family routing and checked runtime samples do not certify every character, fallback environment or native translation.

motion.name: state-feedback
motion.purpose: Navigation background and text, thumbnail opacity, and action-arrow movement.

motion.name: image-feedback
motion.purpose: Image opacity feedback on inspection triggers.

motion.name: hero-arrival
motion.purpose: Homepage content only, at min-width 961px with no reduced-motion preference; not a global entrance recipe.

motion.name: ambient-film-rate
motion.purpose: Both defaultPlaybackRate and playbackRate on the muted, inline, looping film; no on-page playback controls. The film remains visible and requests playback regardless of motion preference; autoplay denial keeps a still fallback.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable decorative interface animation and transitions and make scrolling immediate without hiding or pausing the explicitly requested ambient film.

textures.name: archive-paper
textures.purpose: Paper grain from the letter's blank margin, with uneven illumination removed, contrast limited and the crop mirrored. Used on body, masthead, exhibition and footer backgrounds, never on original object photographs. This is derived raster texture, not an AI-generated historical artifact.

ornaments.name: exhibition-border
ornaments.method: Extract the text-free printed bottom edge as a white-alpha PNG, using squared feathering to reach transparency at all four edges. Crop values are fractions of the original image dimensions; feather dimensions are source-raster pixels. CSS supplies the existing accent color through a contained, non-repeating flat mask, without embossed material.
ornaments.use: One border at the purple exhibition entry on Home and Exhibitions only: top 8px, left max(var(--gutter), calc((100% - var(--max)) / 2)), width min(320px, calc(100% - var(--gutter) * 2)), height 24px and opacity .34. Empty absolute pseudo-elements take no pointer events, carry no assistive-technology text and add no padding or layout space. No decorative accents appear on About, Collections, Research, Contact, 404, footers, the film edge or other sections. Existing fades remain unchanged.
ornaments.provenanceLimit: Modern source-derived decoration, not an authenticated historic website border. The original booklet image is unchanged; no new historical date is assigned to this decoration.

artifactLayout.measurements: Read complete images' mount border-box widths and heights before applying writes.
artifactLayout.mediaOffset: --media-offset equals half the difference between the row's tallest mount and the item's mount height.
artifactLayout.scheduling: Batch reads and writes in requestAnimationFrame. A WeakMap width cache makes ResizeObserver ignore height-only changes.
artifactLayout.state: The alignment routine does not reset keyboard focus, collection selection, viewer zoom or viewer scroll.

narrative.overview:
MOFER's original photographs, documents and film lead a quiet editorial museum. The established porcelain-blue palette, pale-blue actions, muted purple exhibition field and real paper grain remain. A denser printed-album treatment pairs flat, fine-edged mounts with smooth fades. A softly feathered printed border marks only the exhibition entry on Home and Exhibitions; sections and reading columns stay open.

Locale-specific serif headings and editorial prose give eight languages a shared reading rhythm; sans-serif controls and captions remain distinct. Names lead, full historical context follows, and captions share the width of their mounts. Equal columns and row-centered images provide newspaper-like density without a literal newspaper layout. The MOFER wordmark over the original film remains the identity anchor.
keyCharacteristics: Unchanged porcelain-blue fields, pale-blue actions and muted purple exhibitions.
Original paper grain and flat printed mounts around contained, untextured artifacts.
Fade-led transitions with a softly feathered border only at exhibition entries.
Script-specific serif headings and prose, distinct from sans-serif interface text.
Equal columns, row-centered images and captions aligned to mount bounds.
Six dedicated pages with English fallback and eight persistent language choices.
Original quarter-speed film; reduced motion removes decorative UI movement.

rules.name: The Quiet Accent Rule
rules.body: Pale blue marks actions, selection, keyboard focus and restrained printed edges against dark surfaces; it does not recolor the historical media.

rules.name: The Script Before Style Rule
rules.body: Use the locale's Source or regional Noto serif for editorial headings and prose, its sans-serif for interface text, and Bodoni only for MOFER identity lettering.

rules.name: The Title First Rule
rules.body: Give headings and object names priority; place classification and exhibition status below them.

rules.name: The Context Before Count Rule
rules.body: Keep quantities, dates and location facts inside compact labelled notes, not oversized standalone statistics.

rules.name: The Open Gallery Rule
rules.body: Keep sections and reading columns open; flat artifact mounts do not justify colored mats or enclosing text panels.

rules.name: The Mount and Caption Rule
rules.body: Align caption bounds to the mount and center each row's images vertically; do not crop an artifact or reserve an empty fixed-height image stage just to align it.

rules.name: The Flat Gallery Rule
rules.body: Use tonal fields, subtle paper grain and printed edges for depth; keep texture off original object photographs and avoid wood, bevels or gilding.

rules.name: The Fade First Rule
rules.body: Let smooth fades carry transitions; reserve a softly feathered border for the exhibition entry on Home and Exhibitions, with no isolated symbols or repeated page-wide pattern.

dos: Do keep original object images fully visible and free of texture overlays.
Do lead with smooth fades, keep the exhibition border localized and retain flat double-rule mounts around artifact media.
Do align captions to mount bounds and center images within each grid row.
Do place names and headings before type and status metadata.
Do keep reading compact but organized and let all eight languages wrap naturally.
Do use locale-specific serif editorial prose and sans-serif interface text, enlarging readable text independently of graphic identity marks.
Do retain full contextual facts and original meaning while improving text allocation.
Do keep the native language select and explicit preference persistence across dedicated pages.
Do retain visible focus, labelled controls, dialog focus return and motion-preference fallbacks.
Do use build-generated local fonts, existing Lucide icons and original historical media.
donts: Don't add white canvases, ornamental dots or above-title kickers.
Don't turn sections into floating cards or add wood, bevels, gilding, offset shadows or pill controls.
Don't restore colored image mats or enclose reading columns in decorative frames.
Don't spread the exhibition border across the page or add isolated symbols, corner rules or line accents at other section joins.
Don't present the source-derived border as an authenticated historic website border or assign it a new historical date.
Don't replace contextual museum notes with giant standalone numbers or crop documents to fill frames.
Don't add visible film playback controls or promise autoplay when the browser blocks it.
Don't hide or pause the requested film for reduced motion; remove decorative UI animation instead.
Don't invent historical evidence, visitor services or approval and rights claims.
Don't publish upcoming-exhibition placeholders or treat a future poster proposal as a shipped pattern.
Don't use wordmark-sized type in compact controls or scale fonts with viewport width.
Don't replace Lucide icons with glyphs or treat sidecar tonal ramps as site colors.
Don't treat legacy source fonts, borrowed museum branding or failed reference captures as current design authority.
